'''Gonzalo Gerardo Higuaín''' ({{IPA|es|iɣwaˈin|lang}}; born 10 December 1987) is an Argentine professional [[Association football|football]] coach and former [[Football player|player]] who played as a [[Striker (football)|striker]]. He is a player development coach for [[Major League Soccer]] club [[Inter Miami CF|Inter Miami]]. Nicknamed '''''El Pipita''''' or '''''Pipa''''', Higuaín was a prolific striker known for his eye for goal, strong physique, offensive movements and predatory finishing, and is considered to be one of the best strikers of his generation.<ref>{{Cite web| date=4 June 2019|title=5 of the best strikers of the Messi-Ronaldo era|url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/football/5-of-the-best-strikers-of-the-messi-ronaldo-era-sstl|access-date=4 September 2023|website=www. sportskeeda.com|language=en-us}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web| date=5 January 2011|title=Ranking the Top 10 Strikers in World Football: Messi, Eto'o, Tevez, Villa...|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/558798-world-football-ranking-the-top-10-strikers-on-the-planet|access-date=4 September 2023|website=bleacherreport.com|language=en-us}}</ref>

Higuaín started his career with Argentine club [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]], before a transfer to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in January 2007. After lacklustre performances in his first two seasons, Higuaín went on to score 97 goals in his next 146 games for Madrid, and was pivotal in the club's historic 100 points tally in the [[2011–12 La Liga]] title win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=REAL MADRID C.F. - ERROR |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/latest-news/se-cumplen-12-anos-de-la-32-liga-del-real-madrid-02-05-2024 |access-date=2026-06-28 |website=www.realmadrid.com}}</ref> His time in Spain saw him win three [[La Liga]] titles in total. In 2013, Higuaín joined Italian side [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]] for €40 million. in his [[2013–14 SSC Napoli season|first season]], he helped his club win the [[Coppa Italia]], which was only their second domestic honour since 1990. In the [[2015–16 Serie A|2015–16 season]], he was vital in Napoli's title race with [[Juventus FC|Juventus]], scoring 36 goals to win the ''[[Capocannoniere]]'' title and breaking the record for [[Football records and statistics in Italy#Most goals in a single Serie A season|most goals in a Serie A season]].

Italian champions Juventus signed Higuaín for €90 million in 2016, becoming one of the [[List of most expensive association football transfers|most expensive transfers of all time]] and the highest ever transfer for an Italian club. He won [[Double (association football)|domestic doubles]] in his first two seasons with Juventus, also reaching the [[2017 UEFA Champions League final|2017 Champions League final]]. At Juventus, Higuaín scored his 100th goal in Serie A, making him only the second player to score over 100 goals in two of the top European leagues in the past 20 seasons. He went on to have loan spells at [[AC Milan]] and [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], winning the [[UEFA Europa League]] with the latter. He signed for American side [[Inter Miami CF|Inter Miami]] in 2020 before retiring in 2022.<ref>{{cite news |date=3 October 2022 |title=Gonzalo Higuaín to Retire at End of 2022 Campaign |url=https://www.intermiamicf.com/news/gonzalo-higuain-to-retire-at-end-of-2022-campaign |access-date=4 October 2022 |publisher=Inter Miami CF}}</ref>

Born in France to Argentine parents, Higuaín obtained Argentine citizenship in 2007, having previously only been a French national. He made his full international debut for [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] in 2009; he represented the country at three [[FIFA World Cup]]s and three [[Copa América]] tournaments, helping them to second-place finishes at the [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014 World Cup]], the [[2015 Copa América]], and the [[Copa América Centenario]] in 2016. After no longer being called-up following Argentina's round-of-16 exit at the [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018 World Cup]], he announced his retirement from international football in March 2019. In total, he earned 75 caps for his nation, scoring 31 goals.

==Early life==
{{Quote box |width=27% |align=right |quote="[[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]], the Brazilian one, was the best at everything. He is the only player who I have watched on video and tried to imitate, but it's very hard". |source=Higuaín on his idol growing up, Brazil striker Ronaldo.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ronaldo, the Brazilian one, was the best at everything |url=https://en.as.com/en/2017/02/21/football/1487673113_083376.html |last=Candil |first=Jaime |date=21 February 2017 |access-date=10 September 2018 |work=As |archive-date=11 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180911191455/https://en.as.com/en/2017/02/21/football/1487673113_083376.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>}}
Higuaín was born on 10 December 1987 in [[Brest, France]], the son of the Argentine footballer [[Jorge Higuaín]], who was then playing for [[Stade Brestois 29]]. He is of [[Basques|Basque]]-French descent through his grandfather.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euskalkultura.com/espanol/noticias/el-delantero-uruguayo-diego-forlan-su-abuela-vasca-y-sus-deseos-de-fichar-por-el-athletic-club-de-bilbao|title=El delantero uruguayo Diego Forlán, su abuela vasca, y sus deseos de fichar por el Athlétic Club de Bilbao}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lagoutte |first=Alban |date=2020-03-03 |title=Higuain, un Basque à l'Athletic Bilbao ? |url=https://www.sports.fr/football/higuain-basque-a-lathletic-bilbao-335700.html |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=Sports.fr |language=fr-FR}}</ref> He left France at the age of ten months and does not speak French, but retains [[French nationality law|French citizenship]]. He successfully applied for [[Argentine nationality law|Argentine nationality]] in January 2007.<ref name="Higuain to choose Argentina over France">{{cite web|date=24 January 2007|title=Higuain to choose Argentina over France – Report|url=http://www.espnfc.us/story/404406/higuain-to-choose-argentina-over-france-report|access-date=18 October 2015|publisher=ESPN FC}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=5 December 2015|title=Higuain Federico, il fratello di un Dio minore. Ma ora c'è aria di rivincita|url=http://www.repubblica.it/rubriche/la-storia/2015/12/05/news/fratello_higuain_campionato_usa-128800562/|access-date=20 March 2017|publisher=La Repubblica|language=it}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2007-02-08 |title=Higuaín es argentino y Basile puede llamarlo |url=http://www.clarin.com/diario/2007/02/01/deportes/d-04801.htm |access-date=2023-11-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070208085038/http://www.clarin.com/diario/2007/02/01/deportes/d-04801.htm |archive-date=8 February 2007 }}</ref>

Higuaín has two elder brothers, Nicolás, his agent during his career, and [[Federico Higuaín|Federico]], who also played as a professional footballer,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2020/03/02/federico-higuain-signs-dc-united-player-player-development-coach|title=Federico Higuain signs with DC United as player, Player Development Coach|date=2 March 2020|first=Jonathan|last=Sagal}}</ref> and one younger brother, Lautaro.<ref>[http://old.clarin.com/diario/2006/12/04/deportes/d-02001.htm Federico ganó el duelo de los hermanos Higuaín]. Old.clarin.com. Retrieved on 17 April 2014.</ref>

==Club career==
===River Plate===
Higuaín started playing in the youth teams and made his debut with [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]] in a 2–1 defeat against [[Club de Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata|Gimnasia y Esgrima (LP)]] on 29 May 2005.<ref>[http://www.canchallena.com/1193372-higuain-los-convence-a-todos Higuain los convence a todos (Higuain convinces all)] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120226012709/http://www.canchallena.com/1193372-higuain-los-convence-a-todos |date=26 February 2012 }} canchallena.com, 2 November 2009, in Spanish.</ref> On 12 February 2006, he scored his first league goal in a 3–1 victory over [[Club Atlético Banfield|Banfield]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://guardian.touch-line.com/?Lang=0&CTID=29&CPID=68&pStr=Match_List&PLID=191762&ListType=9&TEID=543&Season=2005%20-%202006&mTEID=3375&t=3 |title=Gonzalo Higuaín All goals 2005–2006 (Boca Juniors) |publisher=Guardian Stats |access-date=15 September 2010}}</ref> Higuaín ended the [[2005–06 Argentine Primera División|2005–06 season]] with 5 goals in 12 appearances.<ref name="guardian">{{cite web |url=http://guardian.touch-line.com/?Lang=0&CTID=29&CPID=68&pStr=Player&PLID=191762&TEID=543 |title=Gonzalo Higuaín Facts |publisher=Guardian Stats |access-date=15 September 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101127204526/http://guardian.touch-line.com/?Lang=0&CTID=29&CPID=68&pStr=Player&PLID=191762&TEID=543 |archive-date=27 November 2010  }}</ref>

Following his [[brace (sports)|brace]] in the ''[[Superclásico]]'' [[Local derby|derby]] against [[Boca Juniors]] on 8 October 2006, River Plate manager [[Daniel Passarella]] declared that Higuaín had an "enormous future" and was "destined for superstardom".<ref>{{cite news
| url   = http://www.iht.com/articles/ap/2006/10/09/sports/LA_SPT_SOC_River_Plate_Higuain.php
| title = Passarella predicts River's 18-year-old Higuain has "enormous future"HIGUAIN is becoming one of the most dangerous strikers in the world
| work  = International Herald Tribune |date=9 October 2006
}}</ref> By the end of [[2006–07 Argentine Primera División|that season]], he scored 10 goals in 17 league matches.<ref name="guardian"/>

===Real Madrid===
====2006–07 season====
In December 2006, Spanish club [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] signed Higuaín for [[Euro|€]]12&nbsp;million from River Plate. His debut came on 11 January 2007 against [[Real Betis]] in the second round of the [[Copa del Rey]] in [[Seville]]. His first league game came three days later, on 14 January 2007, against [[Real Zaragoza]] at home. Higuaín was involved in the creation of numerous scoring chances and in the assistance for the only goal, which earned Madrid the victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2007/01/14/spain/primera-division/real-madrid-club-de-futbol/real-zaragoza/389446/|title=Real Madrid vs. Real Zaragoza 1 – 0|publisher=Soccerway|date=14 January 2007|access-date=4 February 2019}}</ref> His first goal with Real came on 24 February when the team faced [[Atlético Madrid]] in the [[Madrid derby]], the equaliser (1–1) at the [[Vicente Calderón Stadium]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2007/02/24/spain/primera-division/club-atletico-de-madrid/real-madrid-club-de-futbol/389502/|title=Atlético Madrid vs. Real Madrid 1 – 1|publisher=Soccerway|date=24 February 2007|access-date=4 February 2019}}</ref> During his first season at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Bernabéu]], however, Higuaín raised some doubts over his performance due to his overall lack of goals.

====2007–08 season====
During the [[2007–08 Real Madrid CF season|2007–08 season]], Higuaín played inconsistently, although he finished strongly at the end of the season: He first scored a last minute goal to earn his team a victory in a 2–1 comeback against [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]], which allowed Real Madrid to be mathematically crowned Liga champions for the second consecutive year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/marcador/futbol/2007_08/primera/jornada_35/osa_rma/asilovivimos.html |title=www.Marca.com |publisher=Marca.com |access-date=31 May 2011}}</ref> Four days later, he scored the third goal of a 4–1 thrashing of [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in ''[[El Clásico]]''. The goal was scored just 57 seconds after he came off the bench.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elpais.com/articulo/deportes/Barca/saca/hombros/Madrid/elpepidep/20080508elpepidep_2/Tes |title=El Barça saca a hombros al Madrid |work=El Pais |date=24 May 2011 |access-date=31 May 2011|last1=Sámano |first1=José }}</ref>

====2008–09 season====
In the [[2008–09 Real Madrid CF season|2008–09 season]], Higuaín was offered the chance to be a starter due to a serious injury suffered by [[Dutch people|Dutch]] striker [[Ruud van Nistelrooy]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elpais.com/articulo/deportes/Higuain/Espero/lesion/Van/Nistelrooy/signifique/retirada/elpepudep/20081113elpepudep_17/Tes |title=Higuaín: "Espero que la lesión de Van Nistelrooy no signifique su retirada" |work=El Pais |date=13 November 2008 |access-date=31 May 2011}}</ref> In August 2008, Higuaín scored the winner in Madrid's victory over [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] in the [[Supercopa de España]].<ref>[http://archivo.marca.com/futbol/2008/supercopa/index.html Supercopa 2008] Marca.com. Retrieved 25 August 2010</ref> Shortly afterwards, he scored all four goals in a 4–3 win against [[Málaga CF|Málaga]]. Because of this, he started to gain international recognition and became one of the leading goalscorers of La Liga, alongside his Barcelona counterpart [[Samuel Eto'o]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sportsnet.ca/soccer/2008/11/08/mardid_malaga_recap/ |title=Higuain, Eto'o both notch four goals |publisher=Sportsnet.ca |date=8 November 2008 |access-date=31 May 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160315014049/http://www.sportsnet.ca/soccer/2008/11/08/mardid_malaga_recap/ |archive-date=15 March 2016 |url-status=dead}}</ref> On 21 April 2009, Higuaín played very well in the match against [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] and scored the decisive goal in the last minute, giving Real Madrid a 3–2 victory which enabled the team to keep close to [[Pep Guardiola]]'s Barcelona in the league table.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.as.com/futbol/articulo/higuain-casillas-especialistas-milagros/20090421dasdasftb_60/Tes |title=Higuaín y Casillas, especialistas en milagros – LIGA BBVA, Real Madrid 3 – Getafe 2 |date=21 April 2009 |publisher=AS.com |access-date=31 May 2011}}</ref> Throughout the season, Higuaín was regarded as one of the most promising talents in world football in the wake of spectacular games and last-minute goals. He ended the season with 22 league goals<ref>[http://soccernet.espn.go.com/stats/topscorers?league=esp.1&year=2008&cc=5901 Spanish Primera División – Top Scorers – 2008/2009] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090207055039/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/stats/topscorers?league=esp.1&year=2008&cc=5901 |date=7 February 2009 }}. ESPN. Retrieved on 16 December 2010</ref> and 24 in all competitions, around as many as established football stars including [[Diego Forlán]], [[David Villa]] and [[Thierry Henry]].

====2009–10 season====
The [[2009–10 Real Madrid CF season|2009–10 season]] saw Higuaín become Real's top goalscorer with 27 league goals, 29 in total, being at the same time the La Liga's second-top goalscorer, behind only [[Lionel Messi]] and surpassing Swedish international [[Zlatan Ibrahimović]], as well as his Madrid teammate [[Cristiano Ronaldo]]. This season included him scoring his first two goals in the [[UEFA Champions League]] and his second [[hat-trick]] for the club.

====2010–11 season====
[[File:Higuaín se prepara para chutar.jpg|thumb|left|Higuaín during a match in the [[2010–11 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] group stage against [[AC Milan]] in October 2010]]

In June 2010, Real Madrid extended Higuaín's contract until 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1193040487639/1330006888664/noticia/ComunicadoOficial/Official_announcement:_Gonzalo_Higuain_s_contract_extended_to_2016.htm |title=Gonzalo Higuain's contract extended to 2016 |publisher=Real Madrid |date=7 June 2010 |access-date=31 May 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110917100632/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1193040487639/1330006888664/noticia/ComunicadoOficial/Official_announcement:_Gonzalo_Higuain_s_contract_extended_to_2016.htm |archive-date=17 September 2011  }}</ref> On 23 October 2010, he scored Real Madrid's 5,200th league goal, coming against [[Racing de Santander]] in a 6–1 thrashing by ''Los Blancos''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en/match/47766/real-madrid-vs-racing/index|title=Real Madrid 6-1 Racing Santander: Cristiano Ronaldo Grabs Four in Rout For Los Merengues|publisher=Goal.com|author=David Schiavone|date=23 October 2010|access-date=5 February 2019}}</ref> On 4 November of the same year, Higuaín scored the club's 700th goal in the Champions League.<ref>{{cite web|author=Champions League |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/1716/champions-league/2010/11/04/2198075/real-madrid-striker-gonzalo-higuain-pleased-to-qualify-for |title=Real Madrid Striker Gonzalo Higuain Pleased To Qualify For Knockout Stages After Milan Draw |publisher=Goal.com |date=4 November 2010 |access-date=31 May 2011}}</ref>

During the first weeks of December 2010, Higuaín was diagnosed with a herniated lumbar disc, and Real's medical staff suggested that he should have it operated.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/real-madrid-wait-for-gonzalo-higuain-injury-assessment-2150267.html | location=London |work=The Independent | title=Real Madrid wait for Gonzalo Higuain injury assessment | date=3 December 2010}}</ref> On 5 January 2011, Real Madrid announced he would finally undergo surgery at the Department of Neurological Surgery of [[Chicago]]'s [[Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine]] under the command of Dr. Richard G. Fessler, [[M.D.]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330033821843/noticia/Noticia/Higuain_will_have_surgery_in_Chicago_on_Tuesday.htm |title=Higuain will have surgery in Chicago on Tuesday |publisher=Real Madrid |date=5 January 2011 |access-date=31 May 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110414095901/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330033821843/noticia/Noticia/Higuain_will_have_surgery_in_Chicago_on_Tuesday.htm |archive-date=14 April 2011  }}</ref> The surgery took place on 11 January, and Higuaín was discharged from the hospital the next day following a successful operation.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330035261223/noticia/Noticia/Higuain_discharged_from_hospital.htm |title=Higuain discharged from hospital |publisher=Real Madrid |date=12 January 2011 |access-date=31 May 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110320135142/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330035261223/noticia/Noticia/Higuain_discharged_from_hospital.htm |archive-date=20 March 2011  }}</ref> He was expected to spend at least four months away from the field in the recovery process: two months spent to recover from the surgery and another two to train with the team, although he was able to make an early comeback. On 23 April 2011, Higuaín scored a hat-trick against [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] in a 6–3 away win at the [[Mestalla Stadium]], giving him eight goals in eight matches against Valencia. Higuaín also assisted two other goals for [[Karim Benzema]] and [[Kaká]] in that same match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en-gb/match/48776/valencia-vs-real-madrid/report|title=Valencia 3-6 Real Madrid: Higuain bags hat-trick & Kaka nets double as visitors win nine-goal thriller|publisher=Goal.com|author=Daniel Quinton-Navarro|date=23 April 2011|access-date=5 February 2019|archive-date=7 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190207020704/https://www.goal.com/en-gb/match/48776/valencia-vs-real-madrid/report|url-status=dead}}</ref>

====2011–12 season====
[[File:Gonzalo Higuaín 48609.jpg|thumb|upright|Higuaín in a Champions League game against [[PFC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] in February 2012]]

On 2 October, Higuaín scored his first hat-trick of the season against Espanyol in a 4–0 away win,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/%2012/spanish-football/2011/10/02/2693483/espanyol-0-4-real-madrid-higuain-hits-hat-trick-callejon|title=Espanyol 0-4 Real Madrid: Higuain hits hat-trick & Callejon nets against old club as capital giants edge to within a point of Barcelona|publisher=Goal.com|author=Ben Hayward|date=2 October 2011|access-date=5 February 2019}}</ref> following it 13 days later with another in a 4–1 win against Betis.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/12/spain/2011/10/15/2712679/real-madrid-4-1-real-betis-higuain-hat-trick-the-highlight|title=Real Madrid 4-1 Real Betis: Higuain hat-trick the highlight as Jose Mourinho's side record comfortable win|publisher=Goal.com|author=Charlie Scott|date=15 October 2011|access-date=5 February 2019}}</ref>

Higuaín scored to put Madrid up 3–1 in a 4–1 win against local rivals Atlético Madrid in the Madrid derby on 26 November. On 31 March 2012, he scored his 100th Real Madrid goal in a match against Osasuna, also adding a second goal to make it Real's 100th goal for the [[2011–12 La Liga]] season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en-au/news/4016/main/2012/04/01/3005516/osasuna-1-5-real-madrid-ronaldo-higuain-at-the-double|title=Osasuna 1-5 Real Madrid: Ronaldo & Higuain at the double & Benzema hits stunner as Mourinho's men make a statement in La Liga|publisher=Goal.com|author=Daniel Quinton-Navarro|date=31 March 2012|access-date=5 February 2019}}</ref> In the league-winning season, he scored 22 goals, more than his teammate [[Karim Benzema]], and proved to be a vital player for his team.<ref>[http://soccernet.espn.go.com/player/_/id/67310/gonzalo-higuain?cc=4716 Higuain statistics] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111020152622/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/player/_/id/67310/gonzalo-higuain?cc=4716 |date=20 October 2011 }}. soccernet.espn.go.com. 27 July 2012</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=46240&season_id=141|title=Games played by Gonzalo Higuain in 2011/2012|publisher=Soccerbase.com|access-date=5 February 2019}}</ref>

====2012–13 season====
[[File:Real Madrid v Sevilla 10 February 2013 A 2.JPG|thumb|left|Higuaín attempting to dribble past [[Emir Spahić]] of [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] in February 2013]]

On 29 August 2012, Higuaín scored the opener in an eventual 2–1 win against Barcelona in the second leg of the [[2012 Supercopa de España]], which secured Real Madrid its first title of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/real-madrid/9507759/Real-Madrid-2-Barcelona-1-4-4-agg-match-report.html|title=Real Madrid 2 Barcelona 1 (4-4 agg): match report|work=The Telegraph|date=30 August 2012|access-date=5 February 2019}}</ref>

Higuaín scored first league goal in the season opener against Valencia CF, his favourite opponent; he netted the opening goal in the 10th minute in an eventual 1–1 home draw.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/r-madrid-vs-valencia/268194|title=Jonas ruins Real opener|publisher=Sky Sports|date=19 August 2012|access-date=5 February 2019}}</ref> He scored again in the next match, a 2–1 loss to [[Getafe CF]] at [[Coliseum Alfonso Pérez]], which marked Real Madrid worst league start in 39 years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/competitions/la-liga/9501656/Real-Madrid-lose-further-ground-in-La-Liga-title-race-on-Barcelona-after-defeat-to-Getafe.html|title=Real Madrid lose further ground in La Liga title race on Barcelona after defeat to Getafe|work=The Telegraph|author=Ed White|date=27 August 2012|access-date=5 February 2019}}</ref>

In Real's away match to [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] on 28 October 2012, Higuaín scored twice and provided two assists in a 5–0 victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://espnfc.com/en/report/348430/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=null |title=Five-star Real hammer Mallorca |publisher=ESPNFC |date=28 October 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130225020241/http://espnfc.com/en/report/348430/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=null |archive-date=25 February 2013  }}</ref> On 23 February 2013, he scored his 100th La Liga goal as he scored an 88th-minute winner to secure a 2–1 defeat of [[Deportivo de La Coruña]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/us/en/report/348285/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5901 |title=Higuain downs Depor |publisher=ESPNFC |date=23 February 2013 }}</ref>

On 1 June 2013, following the end of the team's last match of the season, a 4–2 home win over Osasuna, Higuaín, who scored the opening goal, confirmed that he would be leaving Real Madrid at the end of the season, after six and a half years.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/news/story/_/id/1465718/gonzalo-higuain-confirms-leave-real-madrid|title=Gonzalo Higuain leaving Real Madrid|publisher=ESPN FC|date=2 June 2013|access-date=5 February 2019}}</ref>

===Napoli===
Due to Higuaín's availability in the summer of 2013, several high-profile clubs, such as [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] and [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]], were keen to sign him. Higuaín was at the centre of much transfer speculation, with many newspapers linking him to a move to Premier League side Arsenal, before Napoli's president [[Aurelio De Laurentiis]] said that Higuaín, along with [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] goalkeeper [[Pepe Reina]], had passed their medicals and that the Argentine had signed a five-year deal with the [[Italy|Italian]] club, with Higuaín joining for [[Euro|€]]40&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/news/story?id=1506002&cc=5901 |title=Higuain and Reina pass Napoli medicals |publisher=ESPNFC |date=24 July 2013 |access-date=24 July 2013 }}</ref> On 27 July, Napoli confirmed the signing of Higuaín, with the Argentine being assigned the [[Squad number (association football)|number 9 shirt]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/news/story?id=1508152&cc=5901 |title=Napoli confirm Higuain signing |publisher=ESPNFC |date=27 July 2013 |access-date=27 July 2013 }}</ref>

====2013–14 season====
On 10 August 2013, Higuaín played his first match as a starter in a pre-season friendly against [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]], scoring his first goal for the club in a 2–1 win. On 25 August, he made his [[Serie A]] debut in a 3–0 defeat of [[Bologna FC 1909|Bologna]] on the opening day of the [[2013–14 Serie A|2013–14 season]].<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/soccer/news/20130825/napoli-benitez-serie-a.ap/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140416174735/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/soccer/news/20130825/napoli-benitez-serie-a.ap/|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 April 2014|title=Napoli vanquishes Bologna in Rafa Benitez's debut|date=25 August 2013|access-date=15 April 2014|magazine=Sports Illustrated}}</ref> A week later, he opened his goalscoring account in a 4–2 win away at [[AC ChievoVerona|Chievo]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.football-italia.net/SerieA/match/36993|title= Chievo 2 – 4 Napoli|date=31 August 2013|access-date=15 April 2014|work=Football Italia}}</ref> He followed this up with goals in Napoli's next two fixtures: wins over [[Atalanta BC|Atalanta]] at home<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sbnation.com/soccer/2013/9/14/4730856/napoli-vs-atalanta-final-score-2-0-seriea-2013-14|title=Napoli vs Atalanta, Final Score 2–0: Rafa's reserves rescue Napoli|date=14 September 2013|access-date=15 April 2014|work=SBS Nation}}</ref> and [[AC Milan]] at the [[San Siro]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sbnation.com/soccer/2013/9/22/4759446/ac-milan-napoli-final-score-result-report-goals-serie-a-2013|title=AC Milan – Napoli, final score 1–2: Napoli conquer the San Siro|date=22 September 2013|access-date=15 April 2014|work=SBS Nation}}</ref>

On 18 September, Higuaín scored in Napoli's opening [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] fixture, a 2–1 victory over [[Borussia Dortmund]] at the [[Stadio San Paolo]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/020d-0e863beb7a83-af0b18cf875e-1000--napoli-hold-on-to-see-off-ten-man-dortmund/|title=Napoli hold on to see off ten-man Dortmund|date=18 September 2013|access-date=15 April 2014|work=UEFA}}</ref> He went on to score in home wins over [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]]<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2011810--napoli-vs-marseille/|title=Napoli make their mark in Marseille|date=22 October 2013|access-date=15 April 2014|work=UEFA}}</ref> and Arsenal,<ref name=vain>{{cite news|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2011842--napoli-vs-arsenal/|title=Napoli victory in vain as Arsenal finish second|date=11 December 2013|access-date=15 April 2014|work=UEFA}}</ref> but Napoli failed to qualify from the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League group stage|group stage]] despite winning four of their six matches.<ref name=vain/>

On 12 February 2014, Higuaín scored two goals in Napoli's 3–0 defeat of [[AS Roma|Roma]] in the semi-final of the [[2013–14 Coppa Italia|Coppa Italia]], taking the team to the final with a 5–3 aggregate victory.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sbnation.com/soccer/2014/2/12/5405898/napoli-roma-2014-coppa-italia-final-score-result|title=Napoli vs AS Roma, 2014 Coppa Italia: Final score 3–0, Napoli set up Fiorentina final|date=12 February 2014|access-date=15 April 2014|work=SBS Nation}}</ref> On 13 April, he scored his first hat-trick for the club in a 4–2 win over [[SS Lazio|Lazio]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sbnation.com/2014/4/13/5610314/napoli-vs-lazio-serie-a-2014-final-score-result|title=Napoli vs Lazio, final score 4–2: Higuain treble sinks Lazio|date=13 April 2014|access-date=15 April 2014|work=SBS Nation}}</ref> Higuaín won his first trophy with the club on 3 May, playing for 70 minutes in the 3–1 success versus [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] in the [[2014 Coppa Italia Final|final of Coppa Italia]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/27271913|title=Coppa Italia final: Rafael Benitez's Napoli beat Fiorentina 3-1|website=BBC Sport|date=3 May 2014|access-date=7 February 2019}}</ref> He concluded his first season in [[Italy]] by scoring 24 goals in 46 appearances in all competitions.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=46240&season_id=143|title=Games played by Gonzalo Higuain in 2013/2014|publisher=Soccerbase|access-date=7 February 2019}}</ref>

====2014–15 season====
[[File:Dnepr-Napoli (3).jpg|thumb|Higuaín in action against [[FC Dnipro Dnipropetrovsk|Dnipro]] in May 2015]]

On 26 October 2014, Higuaín scored his first three league goals of the season in a 6–2 home win over [[Hellas Verona FC|Hellas Verona]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Tooth|first1=John-Paul|title=Napoli 6–2 Hellas Verona: Higuain hat-trick helps Benitez's men to big win|url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/napoli-vs-hellas-verona/1836251/report|access-date=26 October 2014|work=Goal.com|date=26 October 2014}}</ref> In the [[2014 Supercoppa Italiana]] against [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in [[Doha]], [[Qatar]], on 22 December, Higuaín equalised twice, forcing extra time and then a [[penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shootout]], in which he was one of the scorers in a Napoli victory.<ref>{{cite news|title=Juventus 2–2 Napoli (5–6 on pens)|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30582475|access-date=22 December 2014|website=BBC Sport|date=22 December 2014}}</ref>

Higuaín scored a hat-trick, including a penalty, on 12 March 2015, as Napoli came from behind to defeat [[FC Dynamo Moscow|Dynamo Moscow]] 3–1 in the first leg of the last 16 of the [[2014–15 UEFA Europa League|UEFA Europa League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Higuaín inspires Napoli comeback against Dinamo|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/match/2014612--napoli-vs-dynamo-moscow/|access-date=13 March 2015|publisher=UEFA|date=12 March 2015}}</ref>

In the final game of the league season – and also the last under Napoli manager [[Rafael Benítez]] – Higuaín scored twice, but also missed a penalty, as Napoli lost 4–2 to Lazio, who took the last Champions League place at their expense.<ref>{{cite news|title=Serie A Review: Napoli miss Champions League in Benitez send-off|url=http://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/serie-review-napoli-miss-champions-league-benitez-send|access-date=3 June 2015|work=[[FourFourTwo]]|date=31 May 2015}}</ref>

====2015–16 season====
On 8 November 2015, Higuaín recorded the 200th goal of his club career, the only goal of the match in a victory over [[Udinese Calcio|Udinese]]; this was his ninth goal of the league season and his seventh consecutive home game with a goal.<ref>{{cite news|title=Napoli, Higuain oltre i 200 gol: "Sogno lo scudetto". Sarri: "No, io il 3° posto"|trans-title=Napoli, Higuaín on 200 goals: "I dream of the ''scudetto''". Sarri: "No, I dream of 3rd place"|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Serie-A/Napoli/08-11-2015/napoli-higuain-va-oltre-200-gol-voglio-titolo-col-napoli-130843519349.shtml|access-date=12 November 2015|work=Gazzetta dello Sport|date=8 November 2015|language=it}}</ref> Three weeks later, he scored both goals – including one after 64 seconds – in a 2–1 win over Inter which put Napoli in first place in the league for the first time in 25 years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/planet-futbol/2015/11/30/napoli-inter-milan-higuain-italy-serie-a|title=Napoli beats Inter Milan, takes first in Serie A|date=30 November 2015 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34899294|title=Napoli 2–1 Inter Milan|website=BBC Sport|date=30 November 2015|access-date=1 December 2015}}</ref>

Higuaín scored twice in Napoli's 3–1 win over [[US Sassuolo Calcio|Sassuolo]] on 16 January 2016 to extend the team's lead to four points; his second goal of the game was his 20th of the campaign.<ref>{{cite news|title=Napoli 3–1 Sassuolo|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35327608|access-date=17 January 2016|website=BBC Sport|date=16 January 2016}}</ref> He scored his 30th goal of the Serie A season in a 3–1 away defeat to Udinese on 3 April, although he was sent off later during the match.<ref>{{cite web|title=Higuain and Napoli fall apart|url=http://www.football-italia.net/82265/higuain-and-napoli-fall-apart|publisher=Football Italia|access-date=3 April 2016|date=3 April 2016}}</ref> In the following days, the Serie A issued a four-match ban against Higuaín; a one-game ban for his two yellow cards, one for "protesting against the match officials", one for "misconduct against an opponent" and one for appearing to push referee [[Massimiliano Irrati]], as well as a [[Euro|€]]20,000 fine.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/82362/higuain-ban-confirmed|title=Higuain ban confirmed|publisher=Football Italia|date=5 April 2016|access-date=5 April 2016}}</ref> On 15 April, following an appeal on his ban, it was reduced to three matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/82854/higuain-ban-reduced|title=Higuain ban reduced|publisher=Football Italia|date=15 April 2016|access-date=16 April 2016}}</ref>

On 14 May, Higuaín scored a hat-trick in a 4–0 home win over [[Frosinone Calcio|Frosinone]] in the final match of the season to win the ''[[Capocannoniere]]'' with 36 total goals, achieving the record for goals in a Serie A season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/84347/higuain-i-am-so-happy|title=Higuain: 'I am so happy!'|publisher=Football Italia|date=14 May 2016|access-date=14 May 2016}}</ref><ref name=goal>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/723/serie-a/2016/05/14/23529832/higuain-makes-serie-a-history-by-breaking-66-year-old|title=Higuain makes Serie A history by breaking 66-year-old goalscoring record|publisher=goal.com|first=Chris|last= Davie|date=14 May 2016|access-date=14 May 2016}}</ref> No other player in the league surpassed 20 goals for the season, with the league's second-topscorer being [[Paulo Dybala]] with 19.<ref name=goals2015-16>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.us/italian-serie-a/12/statistics/scorers?season=2015|title=Serie A Statistics 2015–16|publisher=ESPN FC|date=14 May 2016|access-date=14 May 2016}}</ref>

===Juventus===
====2016–17 season====
[[File:Gonzalo Higuain 2017 (edited).jpg|thumb|right|200px|Higuaín playing for [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in 2017]]

After a month of transfer speculation, on 26 July 2016, Higuaín transferred to rivals [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] for a fee of €90 million paid in two installments, making him the most expensive South American footballer of all time (until [[Neymar]]'s transfer to [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] in 2017); his transfer fee was the highest ever paid by an Italian team (until [[Cristiano Ronaldo]]'s transfer to Juventus in 2018) and also the highest of a player transferring within any domestic league (until [[Kylian Mbappé]]'s transfer to Paris Saint-Germain in 2018).<ref name="Gonzalo Higuaín: Argentina Striker joins Juventus from Napoli">{{cite web|date=26 July 2016|title=Gonzalo Higuain: Argentina striker joins Juventus from Napoli|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/36874091|access-date=26 July 2016|website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=26 July 2016|title=Higuain joins Juventus|url=http://www.juventus.com/en/news/news/2016/higuain-joins-juventus-.php|access-date=26 July 2016|publisher=juventus.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=26 July 2016|title=Gonzalo Higuain's £75m Juventus move – its place in history and what it means for football|url=http://asia.eurosport.com/football/serie-a/2015-2016/gonzalo-higuain-s-78m-juventus-move-its-place-in-history-and-what-it-means-for-football_sto5699162/story.shtml|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160730174220/http://asia.eurosport.com/football/serie-a/2015-2016/gonzalo-higuain-s-78m-juventus-move-its-place-in-history-and-what-it-means-for-football_sto5699162/story.shtml|url-status=dead|archive-date=30 July 2016|access-date=26 July 2016|publisher=eurosport.com}}</ref> Three days after his move, Higuaín stated that his reason for moving to Juventus was because of his relationship with Napoli's chairman [[Aurelio De Laurentiis]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/story/2919594/juventus-gonzalo-higuain-i-left-napoli-because-of-aurelio-de-laurentiis |title=Juventus' Gonzalo Higuain: I left Napoli because of Aurelio De Laurentiis |date=29 July 2016 |publisher=ESPN }}</ref><ref name="Juventus F.C. Profile">{{cite web|url=http://www.juventus.com/en/teams/first-team/forwards/gonzalo-gerardo-higuain-/index.php|title=GONZALO GERARDO HIGUAIN|publisher=juventus.com|access-date=19 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170925181637/http://www.juventus.com/en/teams/first-team/forwards/gonzalo-gerardo-higuain-/index.php|archive-date=25 September 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 20 August, Higuaín scored the winning goal on his Juventus debut in their opening match against [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] of a 2–1 home win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/90108/higuain-happy-juve-goal|title=Higuain: 'Happy with Juve goal'|publisher=Football Italia|date=20 August 2016|access-date=21 August 2016}}</ref> On 10 September, he scored a brace in a 3–1 home win over Sassuolo.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/91239/higuain-and-pjanic-inspire-juventus|title=Higuain and Pjanic inspire Juventus|publisher=Football Italia|date=10 September 2016|access-date=10 September 2016}}</ref> On 29 October, he scored the winning goal against his former team, Napoli, but [[Goal celebration#Notable non-celebrations|did not celebrate his goal]], in a 2–1 home win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/93640/higuain-completes-napoli-nightmare|title=Higuain completes Napoli nightmare|publisher=Football Italia|date=29 October 2016|access-date=29 October 2016}}</ref> On 5 April 2017, Higuaín scored twice against Napoli in the [[2016–17 Coppa Italia]] second semi-final leg to put Juventus through to the [[2017 Coppa Italia Final|final]] 5–4 on aggregate, in spite of a 3–2 away loss.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/100705/coppa-higuain-ends-napoli-hopes|title=Coppa: Higuain ends Napoli hopes|publisher=Football Italia|date=5 April 2017|access-date=5 April 2017}}</ref> The following week, he became the first player to score more than 20 goals in his debut season for Juventus since [[John Charles]] and [[Omar Sívori]] had managed the same feat during the [[1957–58 Serie A]] season, when he scored a brace against [[AC ChievoVerona|Chievo]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/100947/serie-week-31-did-you-know|title=Serie A Week 31: Did You Know?|website=Football Italia|last=Campanale|first=Susan|date=10 April 2017|access-date=20 April 2017}}</ref> On 15 April, Higuaín scored both goals in a 2–0 away win against [[Delfino Pescara 1936|Pescara]], which included his 200th league goal in Europe.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thescore.com/news/1281069|title=Higuain hits 200-goal milestone to push Juventus closer to another title|publisher=The Score|author1=Gianluca Nesci|date=16 April 2017|access-date=17 April 2017}}</ref> On 3 June, Higuaín started in the [[2017 UEFA Champions League Final|Champions League Final]], but Juventus were defeated 4–1 by defending champions, Higuaín's former club, Real Madrid; he set up [[Mario Mandžukić]]'s temporary equaliser in the first half.<ref name="Guardian">{{cite news |date=3 June 2017 |title=Real Madrid and Cristiano Ronaldo see off Juventus to win Champions League |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/jun/03/juventus-real-madrid-champions-league-final-match-report |work=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=3 June 2017}}</ref>

====2017–18 season====
On 28 October 2017, Higuaín scored both goals in a 2–0 away win over Milan; his first goal was his 100th goal in Serie A, making him only the second player after Zlatan Ibrahimović to score over 100 goals in two of the top European leagues in the past 20 seasons.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/club/juventus/111/blog/post/3249665/gonzalo-higuain-produces-a-9-10-display-to-help-juventus-see-off-ac-milan|title=Gonzalo Higuain produces a 9/10 display to help Juve see off Milan|publisher=ESPN FC|author1=Mina Rzouki|date=28 October 2017|access-date=29 October 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://theworldgame.sbs.com.au/article/2017/10/29/higuain-brings-century-juventus-down-stuttering-ac-milan|title=Higuain brings up century as Juventus down stuttering AC Milan|publisher=theworldgame.sbs.com|date=29 October 2017|access-date=29 October 2017}}</ref>

Higuaín played a decisive role in Juventus's 4–3 aggregate win over [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] in the round of 16 of the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]]. In the first leg, held in Turin on 13 February 2018, he scored both of his side's goals in the opening ten minutes, with his second of the night coming from the penalty spot, although he later also missed another penalty right before half time, which drew criticism in the Italian media, despite his positive overall performance; following a comeback from Tottenham, however, the match eventually ended in a 2–2 draw.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2021683--juventus-vs-tottenham/|title=Juventus 2–2 Tottenham|publisher=[[UEFA]]|author1=Paolo Menicucci|author2=Daniel Thacker|date=13 February 2018|access-date=9 March 2018}}</ref> In the return leg, on 7 March, he helped Juventus come from behind to win the match 2–1 at [[Wembley Stadium]], first scoring the equaliser, before setting up the match winner scored by Dybala three minutes later, thus sealing Juventus's place in the quarter-finals of the competition.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/43306558|title=Tottenham Hotspur 1–2 Juventus|website=BBC Sport|author1=Phil McNulty|date=7 March 2018|access-date=9 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/tottenham-juventus-champions-league-match-report-paulo-dybala-gonzalo-higuain-a8244981.html|title=Paulo Dybala and Gonzalo Higuain stun Tottenham to send Juventus into Champions League quarter-finals|work=The Independent|author1=Luke Brown|date=8 March 2018|access-date=9 March 2018}}</ref>

====2018–19 season: Loans to AC Milan and Chelsea====
[[File:Chelsea 3 Sheffield Wednesday 0 (46185950194) (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|upright|Higuaín on loan at [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in 2019]]
On 2 August 2018, Higuaín was signed by [[AC Milan]] on a season-long loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/125650/official-milan-sign-higuain-caldara|title=Official: Milan sign Higuain, Caldara|publisher=Football Italia|date=2 August 2018}}</ref> As per the official statement of [[Juventus FC|Juventus]], Milan would pay a loan fee of €18 million to Juventus in the 2018–19 season; also Milan would have the option to outright buy Higuaín the following season for €36 million.<ref>{{Cite press release|url=http://www.juventus.com/media/native/investor-relations-docs/comunicato%2002082018%20accordi%20con%20milan%20ita.pdf|title=ACCORDI CON IL MILAN|date=2 August 2018|location=Turin|publisher=Juventus F.C.|access-date=16 March 2020|archive-date=2 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180802200231/http://www.juventus.com/media/native/investor-relations-docs/comunicato%2002082018%20accordi%20con%20milan%20ita.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 23 January 2019, English club [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] signed Higuaín on a loan deal for the remainder of the [[2018–19 Chelsea F.C. season|2018–19 season]], reuniting him with manager [[Maurizio Sarri]], whom he played under at Napoli during the [[2015–16 SSC Napoli season|2015–16 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2019/1/23/gonzalo-higuain-completes-loan-transfer-to-chelsea?cardIndex=0-0|title=Gonzalo Higuaín completes loan transfer to Chelsea|publisher=[[Chelsea F.C.]] official website|date=23 January 2019|access-date=23 January 2019}}</ref> Five days later, he made his debut in a 3–0 win against [[Sheffield Wednesday]] in the fourth round of the [[FA Cup]] at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en-au/match/chelsea-v-sheffield-wednesday/report/e95luqqdgq97hrocavvwhhtuy|title=Chelsea 3 Sheffield Wednesday 0: Bayern target Hudson-Odoi nets on Higuain debut|publisher=Goal.com|date=28 January 2019}}</ref> On 30 January, he made his league debut in a 4–0 away loss against [[AFC Bournemouth]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2019/1/30/report|publisher=chelseafc.com|title=REPORT: BOURNEMOUTH 4 CHELSEA 0|date=30 January 2019}}</ref> On 2 February, he scored his first goals for Chelsea, a brace in a 5–0 home win over [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/47011453 |title=Chelsea 5–0 Huddersfield Town |website=BBC Sport |author1=Matt Davis |date=2 February 2019 |access-date=3 February 2019 }}</ref>

====2019–20 season: Return to Juventus====
On 1 July 2019, Higuaín returned to Juventus as Chelsea declined to extend his loan; thus, he was once again reunited with manager Maurizio Sarri, who had recently joined the club.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/international-football/2019/07/01/5d1a205ae2704ea35d8b45f3.html |title=Higuain returns to Juventus as Chelsea turn down purchase option |publisher=Marca |last1=Kostopoulos |first1=Panos |date=1 July 2019 |access-date=16 September 2019 }}</ref> Although he previously wore the number 9 shirt at Juventus, he was instead handed the number 21 shirt ahead of the [[2019–20 Juventus FC season|2019–20 season]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.calciomercato.com/en/news/juve-reveal-new-shirt-numbers-higuain-takes-21-9-ready-for-icard-36302 |title=Juve reveal new shirt numbers: Higuain takes 21, 9 ready for Icardi? |publisher=calciomercato.com |date=19 July 2019 |access-date=16 September 2019 |archive-date=20 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190720130314/https://www.calciomercato.com/en/news/juve-reveal-new-shirt-numbers-higuain-takes-21-9-ready-for-icard-36302 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He scored his first goal of the season in a 4–3 home win over his former club Napoli in Serie A on 31 August.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/49537181 |title=Juventus–Napoli 4–3 |website=BBC Sport |last1=Begley |first1=Emlyn |date=31 August 2019 |access-date=1 September 2019 }}</ref>

On 17 September 2020, he mutually terminated his contract with Juventus.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Thank you for everything, Pipita!|url=https://www.juventus.com/en/news/articles/thanks-for-everything-pipita|access-date=2020-09-17|website=Juventus}}</ref>

===Inter Miami===
On 18 September 2020, Higuaín signed for [[Major League Soccer]] club [[Inter Miami CF|Inter Miami]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Inter Miami CF Signs Forward Gonzalo Higuaín as Designated Player|url=https://www.intermiamicf.com/en/post/2020/09/18/inter-miami-cf-signs-forward-gonzalo-higua-n-designated-player|date=18 September 2020|access-date=18 September 2020|website=Inter Miami CF}}</ref> On his debut, he missed a penalty and then started a fight as Miami fell to a 3–0 defeat to the [[Philadelphia Union]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2020/09/27/heres-how-gonzalo-higuain-fared-his-inter-miami-debut|title=Here's how Gonzalo Higuain fared on his Inter Miami debut|website=Major League Soccer|date=27 September 2020|access-date=28 September 2020}}</ref> On 7 October, Higuaín scored his first goal for Miami, a late free kick in their 2–1 win against the [[New York Red Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2020/10/07/gonzalo-higuain-scores-first-mls-goal-inter-miami-stunning-free-kick-golazo|title=Gonzalo Higuain scores first MLS goal for Inter Miami with stunning free kick golazo|website=Major League Soccer|date=7 October 2020|access-date=8 October 2020}}</ref> On 31 July 2022, Higuaín scored another free-kick for Inter Miami, and then netted two more goals to complete a first-half hat-trick in 27 minutes against [[FC Cincinnati]] in a 4–4 draw.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://en.as.com/soccer/gonzalo-higuain-smashes-27-minute-hat-trick-for-inter-miami-n/ |title=Gonzalo Higuaín smashes 27-minute hat-trick for Inter Miami |language=en-GB |website=en.as.com |date=31 July 2022 |access-date=20 June 2023 }}</ref> Higuaín retired at the end of Inter Miami's 2022 MLS season; his last game was in the first round of the [[MLS playoffs]], ending in 3–0 away loss to [[New York City FC]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Higuain to retire at end of 2022 MLS campaign |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63124702 |access-date=2022-10-18}}</ref>

==International career==
===Early career===
Higuaín is one of only four foreign-born players to have played for Argentina in a [[FIFA World Cup]], along with [[Pedro Arico Suárez]]<ref>{{FIFA player|58521|Pedro Arico Suárez}}</ref>, [[Constantino Urbieta Sosa]]<ref>{{FIFA player|59281|Constantino Urbieta Sosa}}</ref> and [[Nico Paz]]. He initially rejected calls from both the [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] and [[France national football team|France national teams]],<ref>{{cite news
 |url         = http://www.ole.clarin.com/jsp/v4/pagina.jsp?pagId=01306412&fecha=20061110
 |title       = La Celeste y Blanca pesa
 |publisher   = [[Diario Olé|Olé]]
 |date        = 10 November 2006
 |language    = es
 |url-status     = dead
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20061114043839/http://www.ole.clarin.com/jsp/v4/pagina.jsp?pagId=01306412&fecha=20061110
 |archive-date = 14 November 2006}}</ref><ref>{{cite news
| url       = http://www.uefa.com/competitions/EURO/news/Kind=1/newsId=477168.html
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20071014084422/http://www.uefa.com/competitions/EURO/news/Kind%3D1/newsId%3D477168.html
| url-status = dead
| archive-date = 14 October 2007
| title     = Domenech turns to uncapped tyros
| publisher = [[UEFA]]
| date      = 9 November 2006
}}</ref> stating at the time he had not yet decided which country he would play for, before ultimately choosing Argentina.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/sow/news?slug=reu-spainhiguain&prov=reuters&type=lgns "Higuain to choose Argentina over France"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200819002958/https://sports.yahoo.com/soccer/ |date=19 August 2020 }} – Yahoo sports</ref> Higuaín was called up by the [[Argentina Olympic football team|Argentina Olympic squad]] for a friendly match against [[Guatemala national football team|Guatemala]] in February 2008,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lanacion.com.ar/nota.asp?nota_id=985239 |title=Higuaín called up for friendly against Guatemala |publisher=Lanacion.com.ar |access-date=26 June 2010 |archive-date=19 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200819003010/https://www.lanacion.com.ar/deportes/la-argentina-olimpica-se-lucio-ante-guatemala-nid985239/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> and scored two goals on his debut as Argentina won 5–0, though the match was not officially recognized by [[FIFA]] as an "A" international match.

===2010 FIFA World Cup===
[[File:FIFA World Cup 2010 Argentina South Korea2.jpg|thumb|right|300px| Higuaín (#9) [[Goal celebration|celebrates]] his [[hat-trick]] against [[South Korea national football team|South Korea]] with teammates during the [[FIFA World Cup 2010|World Cup]] on 17 June 2010.]]

Higuaín was selected for Argentina by coach [[Diego Maradona]] for the last [[2010 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)|2010 FIFA World Cup qualification games]] against [[Peru national football team|Peru]] and [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]]. He scored his first goal on his full debut, a 49th-minute strike during a 2–1 win over Peru on 10 October 2009. Following Argentina's qualification, Higuaín was included in the squad for the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]]. He scored a hat-trick in Argentina's 4–1 win over [[South Korea national football team|South Korea]] in their second group match,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2010/matches/match_18/default.stm|title=Argentina 4–1 South Korea|date=17 June 2010|website=BBC Sport |first=Jonathan|last=Stevenson|access-date=17 June 2010}}</ref> becoming the third Argentinian to score a hat-trick in the World Cup finals after [[Guillermo Stábile]] in [[1930 FIFA World Cup|1930]] and [[Gabriel Batistuta]] in [[1994 FIFA World Cup|1994]] and [[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998]],<ref>{{cite news|author=Richard Williams|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2010/jun/17/argentina-south-korea-world-cup-2010 |title=Argentina 4–1 South Korea, World Cup 2010 match report |work=The Guardian |location=UK |date= 17 June 2010|access-date=26 June 2010 }}</ref> and the first player to score a [[hat-trick]] in the tournament since 2002. His goal in the 3–1 win over [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]] in the second round took him to a total of four, sending him clear as the second-top goalscorer in the competition.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2010/jun/27/argentina-mexico-world-cup-2010|title=World Cup 2010: Carlos Tevez drives Argentina to victory over Mexico|work=The Guardian|author=Paul Wilson|date=28 June 2010|access-date=3 February 2019}}</ref>

===2011 Copa América===
Higuaín was a member of [[Sergio Batista]]'s Argentine squad for the [[2011 Copa América]] on home soil, making one substitute appearance and one start in the group as [[Carlos Tevez]] was preferred at centre forward; Argentina advanced in second place behind [[Colombia national football team|Colombia]]. He started against Uruguay in the quarter-finals in [[Santa Fe, Argentina|Santa Fe]], and equalised in the 17th minute by heading Lionel Messi's cross past goalkeeper [[Fernando Muslera]]; he later had another goal disallowed for offside. Higuaín scored in the [[penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] after his shot had hit both posts, but Argentina lost the shoot-out 4–5.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Edwards|first1=Daniel|title=Argentina 1–1 Uruguay (AET, 4–5 pens.): Carlos Tevez penalty miss proves costly as hosts crash out of Copa America|url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/argentina-vs-uruguay/1064737/report|access-date=20 June 2015|publisher=Goal.com|date=17 July 2011}}</ref>

===2011–2014: 2014 World Cup qualifying===
On 8 October 2011, Higuaín scored a hat-trick and assisted one goal in a 4–1 win against [[Chile national football team|Chile]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.deseret.com/2011/10/7/20221613/higuain-gets-3-as-argentina-beats-chile-4-1/|title=Higuain gets 3 as Argentina beats Chile 4-1|publisher=Deseretnews.com|author=Vicente Panetta|date=7 October 2011|access-date=5 February 2019}}</ref> On 2 June 2012, he scored the second goal in their [[2014 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)|2014 World Cup qualifying]] match and assisted one goal in Argentina's 4–0 victory over [[Ecuador national football team|Ecuador]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eluniverso.com/2012/06/02/1/1372/ecuador-humillado-4-0-aplanadora-argentina-buenos-aires.html|title=Ecuador fue humillado 4-0 por una 'aplanadora' argentina en Buenos Aires|publisher=Eluniverso.com|language=es|date=2 June 2012|access-date=5 February 2019}}</ref>

On 7 September 2012, Higuaín scored the second goal in their 2014 World Cup South American qualifier match and assisted one goal in Argentina's 3–1 victory over [[Paraguay national football team|Paraguay]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.soccerway.com/matches/2012/09/08/south-america/wc-qualifying-south-america/argentina/paraguay/1172915/|title=Argentina vs. Paraguay 1 – 1|publisher=Soccerway|date=8 September 2012|access-date=9 February 2019}}</ref> Then, on 11 September, Higuaín scored the equalizer for Argentina in a 1–1 draw with Peru in [[Lima]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.emirates247.com/sports/football/higuain-rescues-point-for-subdued-argentina-2012-09-12-1.475181|title=Higuain rescues point for subdued Argentina|publisher=Emirates247.com|date=12 September 2012|access-date=9 February 2019}}</ref>

On 22 March 2013, Higuaín scored twice as Argentina beat [[Venezuela national football team|Venezuela]] 3–0<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/preliminaries/news/newsid=2044048/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130326002707/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/preliminaries/news/newsid=2044048/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=26 March 2013|title=Messi, Higuain power Argentina past Venezuela|date=23 March 2013|publisher=FIFA}}</ref> to make him [[2014 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)#Goalscorers|top scorer]] in the South American section of World Cup qualifying with nine goals. He ended the 2014 qualifying campaign as the joint third-top scorer in [[CONMEBOL]], alongside [[Radamel Falcao]] and behind Messi and [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/preliminaries/southamerica/statistics/topscorers.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071117162558/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/preliminaries/southamerica/statistics/topscorers.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 November 2007|title=2014 FIFA World Cup Brazil Preliminaries: South America: Top Scorers|access-date=22 June 2014|publisher=FIFA}}</ref>

===2014 World Cup===
[[File:Germany and Argentina face off in the final of the World Cup 2014 -2014-07-13 (36).jpg|thumb|left|Higuaín challenging Germany's [[Mats Hummels]] and [[Manuel Neuer]] in the [[2014 FIFA World Cup Final|2014 World Cup Final]]]]
Higuaín was named by manager [[Alejandro Sabella]] in Argentina's 23-man squad for the [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014 World Cup]] in May.<ref>{{cite news|title=World Cup 2014: Argentina leave out Carlos Tevez and Erik Lamela|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27403312|access-date=21 May 2014|website=BBC Sport|date=13 May 2014}}</ref> After appearing as a half-time substitute in Argentina's 2–1 defeat of [[Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team|Bosnia and Herzegovina]] at the [[Maracanã Stadium]] on 15 June, Higuaín exchanged passes with Messi to assist his captain for the winning goal.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/25285099|title=Argentina 2–1 Bos-Herce|date=16 June 2014|access-date=21 June 2014|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He was named in the starting line-up for the team's second match against [[Iran national football team|Iran]] in [[Belo Horizonte]] on 21 June, which ended in a 1–0 victory to Argentina.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/25285221|title=Argentina vs Iran|date=21 June 2014|access-date=22 June 2014|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 5 July, he scored the only goal of the match in the 1–0 [[2014 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Quarter-finals|quarter-final]] victory over [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/28069209|title=Argentina 1–0 Belgium|access-date=6 June 2014|date=5 June 2014|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> In [[2014 FIFA World Cup Final|the final]] against Germany on 13 July, Higuaín shot wide on a one-on-one chance against Germany goalkeeper [[Manuel Neuer]] after being gifted an errant, headed back-pass from [[Toni Kroos]], and had a goal disallowed for [[Offside (association football)|offside]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2014/07/13/gonzalo-higuain-miss-argentina-world-cup_n_5582561.html|title=Gonzalo Higuain Missed Argentina's Best Chance Against Germany (VIDEO/GIF)|date=13 July 2014|access-date=15 July 2014|work=Huffington Post}}</ref> as Germany eventually won the match 1–0 in extra time.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/jul/13/germany-argentina-world-cup-final-2014-match-report|title=Germany beat Argentina to win World Cup final with late Mario Götze goal|date=14 July 2014|access-date=15 July 2014|work=The Guardian}}</ref>

===2015 Copa América===
With [[Sergio Agüero]] preferred as the lone centre-forward in a three-man Argentine attack, Higuaín made his first start of the [[2015 Copa América]] in the final [[2015 Copa América Group B|group]] match, against [[Jamaica national football team|Jamaica]] in [[Viña del Mar]]. Winning his 50th cap, he scored the only goal of the game in the 11th minute when set up by [[Ángel Di María]], sending Argentina through to the quarter-finals as group winners.<ref>{{cite news|title=Gonzalo Higuain's goal helps Argentina finish atop Group B|url=http://www.espnfc.com/copa-america/match/409841/argentina-jamaica/report|access-date=20 June 2015|publisher=ESPN|date=20 June 2015}}</ref> On 30 June, he scored the final goal of Argentina's 6–1 win over Paraguay in the semi-finals, two minutes after coming on in place of Agüero.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Emons|first1=Michael|title=Argentina 6–1 Paraguay|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33085956|access-date=1 July 2015|website=BBC Sport|date=1 July 2015}}</ref> On 4 July, Higuaín was one of two Argentina players to fail to convert their kicks in a penalty shootout loss to [[Chile national football team|Chile]] in the [[2015 Copa América Final]], blasting his attempt over the crossbar; during regulation time he had previously been provided with a late goalscoring opportunity, but failed to convert [[Ezequiel Lavezzi]]'s low cross.<ref name="Higuain's grim record in finals"/><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/33085977|title=Chile 0–0 Argentina|website=BBC Sport|date=5 July 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/jul/05/chile-argentina-copa-america-final-match-report|title=Hosts Chile stun Argentina to claim first Copa América title on penalties|work=The Guardian|author1=Jonathan Wilson|date=5 July 2015|access-date=12 June 2017}}</ref>

===Copa América Centenario===
[[File:Higuaín 20180626.jpg|200px|thumb|Higuaín with [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] at the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]]]]

At the [[Copa América Centenario]] in 2016, Higuaín was named to [[Gerardo Martino]]'s 23-man Argentina squad, and was selected as his team's starting centre forward.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/argentina/story/2876914/carlos-tevez-paulo-dybala-left-off-argentinas-copa-america-squad|title=Carlos Tevez, Paulo Dybala left off Argentina's Copa America squad|publisher=ESPN FC|date=20 May 2016|access-date=31 May 2016}}</ref> On 18 June, he scored twice in the team's 4–1 quarter-final defeat of Venezuela.<ref name=MOTM-ARG-VEN>{{cite web|url=http://www.ca2016.com/matches/27|title=Match 27 : Argentina vs Venezuela|publisher=[[Copa América Centenario]]|date=18 June 2016|access-date=18 June 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160618000735/http://www.ca2016.com/matches/27|archive-date=18 June 2016}}</ref> Three days later, he once again scored two goals as Argentina defeated the hosts [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]] 4–0 in the semi-final.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/36593966|title=Lionel Messi breaks record as Argentina reach Copa America final|date=22 June 2016|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He played in the [[Copa América Centenario Final|final]] against Chile eight days later, a repeat of the previous year's final, as the ''Albiceleste'' once again lost in a penalty shootout following a 0–0 draw after extra time. Following the match, Higuaín once again came under criticism in the media for squandering a one on one opportunity for the third consecutive final with Argentina.<ref name="Higuain's grim record in finals"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2016/jun/26/copa-america-2016-final-argentina-chile-live-score|title=Chile beat Argentina on penalties to win Copa América – as it happened|work=The Guardian|author1=Tom Lutz|date=27 June 2016|access-date=11 July 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportsnet.ca/soccer/xxx-wins-copa-america-centenario-title/|title=Argentina falls to Chile in Copa America Centenario final|publisher=Sportsnet.ca|date=26 June 2016|access-date=12 June 2017}}</ref>

===2018 World Cup===
During Argentina's troublesome [[2018 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)|qualifying campaign]] for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]] in Russia, Higuaín managed only one goal in nine appearances, and eventually lost his place in the team's starting line-up.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/players/player/271550/profile/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180702011039/https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/players/player/271550/profile/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=2 July 2018 |title=2018 FIFA World Cup Profile: Gonzalo Higuaín |publisher=FIFA.com |access-date=1 July 2018 }}</ref> In May 2018, however, Higuaín was included in [[Jorge Sampaoli]]'s final 23-man Argentina squad for the tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/world-cup/argentina-world-cup-squad-paulo-dybala-mauro-icardi-a8362096.html |title=Argentina World Cup squad: Paulo Dybala included but Mauro Icardi misses out on 23-man group for Russia |work=The Independent|date=21 May 2018 |access-date=17 June 2018 }}</ref> He appeared in all three group matches for Argentina, but went scoreless throughout the competition, and did not feature in the round of 16 match against eventual champions [[France national football team|France]] on 30 June, which saw Argentina eliminated from the World Cup following a 4–3 defeat.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/live/football/43976007 |title=France 4–3 Argentina |website=BBC Sport |author=Emlyn Begley |date=30 June 2018  |access-date=30 June 2018 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-cup/2018/06/30/france-vs-argentina-world-cup-2018-live-score-lionel-messi-latest/ |title=Kylian Mbappe destroys Argentina to send Lionel Messi and co home in World Cup thriller |work=The Telegraph|author1=Sam Wallace |date=1 July 2018 |access-date=1 July 2018 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/players/player/271550/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180623113136/https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/players/player/271550/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=23 June 2018 |title=Gonzalo Higuaín |publisher=FIFA.com |access-date=1 July 2018 }}</ref><ref name="Nigeria 1–2 Argentina–2018FWC">{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44439263 |title=Nigeria 1–2 Argentina |website=BBC Sport |last=Skelton |first=Jack |date=26 June 2018}}</ref>

===National team retirement===
On 28 March 2019, in an interview with [[Fox Sports (Latin America)|Fox Sports Argentina]], Higuaín announced his retirement from international football, where he defended himself, commenting: "My era with the Selecc[í]on is over, now I will be watching the team from the outside, which I'm sure will make many people happy. So now that you can stop worrying if I'm here or not. I spoke to [[Lionel Scaloni|[Coach Lionel] Scaloni]] and told him my point of view. This is my decision and I think it will do me good. I want to enjoy more time with my family and I see they suffer when I am so roundly criticised. I am happy with the decision I have made. I played almost 8 years in the team, it's a lot, even if people don't take dimension." In total, he made 75 senior appearances for Argentina, scoring 31 goals. His final international appearance came in Argentina's 2–1 win over [[Nigeria national football team|Nigeria]] on 26 June 2018, in their final group match of the 2018 World Cup, at the [[Krestovsky Stadium]], Saint Petersburg.<ref name="Nigeria 1–2 Argentina–2018FWC"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.football-italia.net/136323/higuain-quits-argentina-squad |title=Higuain quits Argentina squad |publisher=Football Italia |date=28 March 2019 |access-date=28 March 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://in.reuters.com/article/soccer-argentina-higuain/soccer-higuain-announces-argentina-retirement-idINKCN1R92J8 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328194947/https://in.reuters.com/article/soccer-argentina-higuain/soccer-higuain-announces-argentina-retirement-idINKCN1R92J8 |url-status=dead |archive-date=28 March 2019 |title=Soccer: Higuain announces Argentina retirement |publisher=Reuters |author1=Richard Martin |author2=Toby Davis |date=28 March 2019 |access-date=28 March 2019 }}</ref>

==Style of play==
Nicknamed ''El Pipita'' or ''Pipa'',<ref name="El Pìpita">{{cite web|date=25 July 2013|title=Alla scoperta di Gonzalo "El Pìpita" Higuain|trans-title=Finding out who Gonzalo "El Pipita" Higuain is|url=http://www.canalenapoli.it/news-napoli/video-alla-scoperta-di-gonzalo-el-pipita-higuain-79155|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20150310000320/http://www.canalenapoli.it/news-napoli/video-alla-scoperta-di-gonzalo-el-pipita-higuain-79155|archive-date=10 March 2015|access-date=9 March 2015|publisher=canalenapoli.it|language=it}}</ref> as was his father [[Jorge Higuaín|Jorge]], who was also a footballer, Higuaín was a hardworking right-footed striker and a prolific goalscorer. He was known in particular for his great striking ability with either foot in the last 25 yards,<ref name=r1>{{cite web|url=http://www.sscnapoli.it/Squadra/Gonzalo-Higuain|title=Prima Squadra – SSC Napoli|access-date=14 February 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150212070151/http://www.sscnapoli.it/Squadra/Gonzalo-Higuain|archive-date=12 February 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="Higuain has the skills to prosper at Chelsea">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/982184 |title=Higuain has the skills to prosper at Chelsea |publisher=Premier League |date=28 January 2019 |access-date=28 March 2019 }}</ref> as well as his opportunism and clinical finishing inside the penalty area, while his height, eye for goal, and strong physique made him a dangerous aerial presence in the box. A well-rounded striker, he also possessed good technical skills, and an ability to drop deep, link-up with teammates, hold up the ball, and lay it off to other players. His intelligent offensive movement off the ball and pace in the final third of the pitch made him an offensive threat during counter-attacks, and also allowed him to lose his markers and get on the end of passes, or create space for his teammates with his attacking runs.<ref name="El Pìpita"/><ref name="Higuain has the skills to prosper at Chelsea"/><ref name="brilliant">{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/024d-0e995cc98462-58a242a1de8a-1000--how-brilliant-is-new-chelsea-signing-gonzalo-higuain/|title=How brilliant is Juventus' Gonzalo Higuaín?|publisher=[[UEFA]]|date=14 March 2017|access-date=15 March 2017}}</ref><ref name="Higuaín Finds Comfort in Columbus">{{cite web|url=http://goal.blogs.nytimes.com/2012/09/14/higuain-finds-comfort-in-columbus/|title=Higuaín Finds Comfort in Columbus|work=The New York Times|author=Eric Beard|date=14 September 2012|access-date=20 March 2017}}</ref><ref name="all-round">{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/club/ac-milan/103/blog/post/3624999/gonzalo-higuains-all-round-play-hints-he-can-bring-more-than-just-goals-to-milan |title=Gonzalo Higuain's all-round play hints he can bring more than just goals to Milan |publisher=ESPN FC |last1=Paul |first1=Sumeet |date=5 September 2018 |access-date=16 September 2019 }}</ref> Although he mainly played as an out-and-out [[Forward (association football)#Striker|striker]] (which led him to be described as a "poacher" in the media earlier on in his career), because of his team-play and ability to build attacks or provide [[Assist (association football)|assists]] for teammates, he also operated in a deeper, more creative role on occasion, acting as a [[Forward (association football)#False 9|false nine]], or even as a [[Forward (association football)#Second striker|second striker]].<ref name="all-round"/><ref name="Loose Vuvuzela">{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/06/22/opinion/22iht-edcohen.html |title=The Loose Vuvuzela |work=The New York Times |last1=Cohen |first1=Roger |date=21 June 2010 |access-date=12 April 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.football-italia.net/116818/crespo-%E2%80%99play-icardi-higuain%E2%80%99 |title=Crespo: 'Play Icardi with Higuain' |publisher=Football Italia |date=6 February 2018 |access-date=2 September 2018 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/arsene-wenger-struggling-juventus-max-10213736 |title=With Arsene Wenger struggling, Juventus' Max Allegri gave Arsenal food for thought with spot-on tactics to stun Barcelona |work=Daily Mirror|author1=Darren Lewis |date=12 April 2017 |access-date=2 September 2018 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pianetamilan.it/focus/cutrone-higuain-la-coppia-funziona-ma/ |title=Cutrone-Higuain: la coppia funziona, ma… |publisher=pianetamilan.it |language=it |last1=Bressi |first1=Stefano |date=3 September 2018 |access-date=15 September 2019 |archive-date=7 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180907204407/http://www.pianetamilan.it/focus/cutrone-higuain-la-coppia-funziona-ma/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> His playing style earned him comparisons with compatriots [[Hernán Crespo]] and [[Gabriel Batistuta]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/3277/la-liga/2011/10/18/2717055/hernan-crespo-real-madrids-gonzalo-higuain-is-my-natural|title=Hernan Crespo: Real Madrid's Gonzalo Higuain is my natural successor in the Argentina national team|website=Goal.com|author1=Daniel Edwards|date=18 October 2011|access-date=11 January 2016}}</ref><ref name="Penpix of likely Argentina squad">{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-soccer-world-penpix-argentina-idUSKBN0DF06J20140429|title=Penpix of likely Argentina squad for World Cup finals|publisher=Reuters|author1=Rex Gowar|date=28 April 2014|access-date=20 March 2017}}</ref>

Despite his impressive scoring record, Higuaín was often criticised in the media for failing to deliver in the most important of matches for both club and country. Notable examples include poor performances in cup finals and crucial [[UEFA Champions League]] and [[UEFA Europa League]] matches during his tenures at Real Madrid, Napoli and Juventus, as well as notable missed chances for the Argentina national team in the [[2014 FIFA World Cup Final|2014 World Cup Final]], the [[2015 Copa América Final]] and the [[Copa América Centenario Final]].<ref name="Higuain's grim record in finals">{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/en/football/international-football/2017/06/05/593573fd46163f84608b45be.html|title=Higuain's grim record in finals|publisher=Marca|author1=Joel del Río|date=5 June 2017|access-date=6 June 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/international-football/2016/06/27/57713b9de2704ea6148b46b0.html |title=Higuain's 10 most catastrophic misses |publisher=Marca |author1=Joel del Río |date=27 June 2016 |access-date=28 March 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.football-italia.net/119347/higuain-master-misses |title=Higuain master of misses |publisher=Football Italia |author1=Susy Campanale |date=3 April 2018 |access-date=28 March 2019 }}</ref><ref name="Higuain, il quarto rigore sbagliato è letale">{{cite web |url=https://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Serie-A/Napoli/31-05-2015/higuain-quarto-rigore-sbagliato-letale-niente-champions-addio-napoli-1101061909025.shtml |title=Higuain, il quarto rigore sbagliato è letale: niente Champions, addio Napoli? |publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport |language=it |author1=Ivan Palumbo |date=31 May 2015 |access-date=28 March 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2019/06/06/5cf8f501e2704e84bd8b459c.html |title=Jovic joins list of great strikers to sign for Real Madrid |publisher=Marca |last1=Hurtado |first1=José Luis |last2=Munday |first2=Billy |date=6 June 2019 |access-date=16 September 2019 }}</ref> Moreover, Higuaín's record from the [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty spot]] was inconsistent throughout his career;<ref name="=Higuaín suffers Milan meltdown">{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/nov/12/gonzalo-higuain-milan-juventus-red-card-serie-a-football |title=Higuaín suffers Milan meltdown as Juventus push him over the edge |work=The Guardian|first=Nicky |last=Bandini |date=12 November 2018 |access-date=28 March 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.foxsports.it/2018/11/12/higuain-errori-decisivi-carriera-rigori-sbagliati/ |title=Tutti gli errori decisivi di Higuain, Pipita d'oro dagli sbagli horror |work=Fox Sports |language=it |author1=Stefano Fiori |date=12 November 2018 |access-date=28 March 2019 }}</ref> in his early career, he was generally an accurate penalty taker,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/alonso-row-with-ronaldo-played-down-1908155.html |title=Alonso row with Ronaldo played down |work=The Independent|date=23 February 2010 |access-date=28 March 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ilnapolista.it/2015/12/napoli-rigori-hamsik-higuain/ |title=Il Napoli di De Laurentiis ha sbagliato 29 rigori (su 75). L'ultimo rigorista è stato Domizzi. Hamsik ne ha falliti nove, Cavani otto |publisher=ilnapolista.it |language=it |author1=Alfonso Fasano |date=22 December 2015 |access-date=28 March 2019 }}</ref> however his ability from spot kicks deteriorated as his career progressed.<ref name="Higuain, il quarto rigore sbagliato è letale"/><ref name="=Higuaín suffers Milan meltdown"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sportmediaset.mediaset.it/calcio/milan/milan-160-higuain-quanti-errori-dal-dischetto-_1246130-201802a.shtml |title=Milan: Higuain, quanti errori dal dischetto! |publisher=Sport Mediaset |author1=ALESSANDRO FRANCHETTI |language=it |date=12 November 2018 |access-date=28 March 2019 }}</ref>

==Endorsements==
Higuaín, along with global cover star Lionel Messi, featured on the Italian cover of [[EA Sports]]' multi-platform video game ''[[FIFA 15]]''.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.easports.com/it/fifa/notizie/2014/fifa-15-svelata-la-cover-italiana-it|title=FIFA 15 – Svelata la Cover Italiana|trans-title=FIFA 15 – Italian Cover revealed|publisher=[[EA Sports]]|language=it|date=30 August 2014|access-date=21 September 2014}}</ref>
